flawed_step: The claim needs every tree with 2-7 vertices to have a single central vertex. In a tree, diam = 2 rad only when the center is one vertex; when the center is two adjacent vertices, diam = 2 rad - 1. Even paths (P2, P4, P6) have two-vertex centers.
counterexample: T = K2 (n=2), the single edge u-v. d(u,v)=1, so diam=1. ecc(u)=ecc(v)=1, so rad=1 and 2rad=2, and 1 != 2. Also P4: diam=3, rad=2 (3 != 4).
assessment_summary: False. Trees satisfy diam in {2rad-1, 2rad}, and paths with an even number of vertices give 2rad-1. The smallest case, K2, has diam 1 and rad 1.
